ExecutiveSummary.Overview: mofcomp.exe compiled a .mof file (excluding known SQL/SCCM contexts) - MOF compilation can install WMI event subscriptions used for persistence. Triage question: is this WMI-persistence installation, or legitimate software/management MOF compilation?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Malicious MOF compilation registers WMI event consumers that survive reboots and run attacker code on triggers.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Mofcomp
Signal.Details: mofcomp.exe compiling a .mof, not the known SQL context.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the MOF compilation installs WMI persistence or is legitimate.

Step.name: Mofcomp command, MOF path and parent
Step.Purpose: The MOF file path and parent process reveal software installation vs attacker persistence.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)mofcomp(.exe)?" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A .mof in temp/appdata or a user-writable path compiled by a script/unknown parent = persistence. A vendor installer compiling its own MOF in Program Files is benign.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: A .mof from a temp/user-writable path compiled by a suspicious parent (script/dropper).
Node.Result: True Positive (WMI Persistence - IR, remove the subscription)

Node.Condition: A vendor installer/management tool compiling its own MOF under a known context.
Mofcomp with an unclear MOF path/parent.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-MOF-DETAIL, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the software; close as false_positive.
Enumerate and remove the WMI event consumer/filter/binding; isolate the host; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A management product using MOF by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
